subject: Physics
topic: 9.1 Image formed by a plane mirror
title: Image Formed by a Plane Mirror
summary: Stand 2 m from a mirror and your image is 4 m from you. Why a plane mirror's image is virtual, erect, the same size, as far behind as you are in front, and laterally inverted.

notes.title: 05 – Image Formed by a Plane Mirror

keyPoints: Rays from an object reflect off the mirror; traced back, they appear to come from one point **behind** the mirror: the image.
The image is as far **behind** the mirror as the object is **in front** (2 m in front → 4 m from you).
It is **virtual** (cannot be caught on a screen) and **erect**, and the **same size** as the object.
It is **laterally inverted**: your right hand appears as the image's left (hence the mirror-written AMBULANCE).

head: Property
Plane mirror
rows: Virtual (cannot be obtained on a screen)
As far behind the mirror as the object is in front

list: Two rays leave the top of the object and strike the mirror.
Each reflects with angle of reflection = angle of incidence.
The reflected rays diverge; the eye traces them straight back.
The dashed extensions meet behind the mirror: the virtual image.

blocks.formula: Object 2 m in front → image 2 m behind → you to image = 2 + 2 = 4 m

blocks.p: If you walk 1 m towards the mirror, the image also moves 1 m towards it, so the distance between you and your image falls by 2 m.

quiz.q: You stand 3 m in front of a plane mirror. Your distance from your image is:
quiz.explain: Image 3 m behind the mirror: 3 + 3 = 6 m.

quiz.q: A plane mirror's image cannot be caught on a screen because it is:
quiz.explain: The reflected rays only appear to meet behind the mirror.

quiz.q: AMBULANCE is written in mirror form on the vehicle's front because of:
quiz.explain: A rear-view mirror inverts it back so drivers read it correctly.

simulation.reason: The reel's ray diagram covers it; ray-tracing simulations come with spherical mirrors.
